description:
The files the harness owns but cannot supply from a classpath, and the manifest saying what a
        project may do with each.

        Most of the harness reaches a project as configuration an analyzer reads off its own plugin
        classpath, which is why most of it needs no file in the project at all. What lands here is what
        something outside Maven reads from disk: an editor reading .editorconfig, git reading
        .gitattributes. Those have nowhere else to live, so they live in the project and are checked
        against the bytes shipped here.

        Each canonical file is stored under an added .asset suffix. A stored .gitignore under its own
        name would be a working .gitignore over this directory and could stop its neighbours from being
        tracked, and a stored .gitattributes would take effect over them. A file that changes the meaning
        of the directory it sits in cannot be stored under its own name.
